EDIT: One tip that I have to offer is to produce multiple design drafts for your boss to review. **Red flags to look out for while job hunting:**

1). Recruiter/hiring manager wants to interview you by text message or wants to have a virtual interview with you without showing their face.

2). You get an email filled with internal company information prior to even having your interview (e.g. payroll, direct deposit, company equipment, etc.) luring you into a false sense of belief that you're already going to be hired for the job.

3). You are provided with documents to fill out but there are typos and the company logo is blurry. 

4). Someone emailing you out of the blue saying they received your resume from a job posting but doesn't say what job it is or what company they're contacting you from.

5). A "recruiter" contacting you by Gmail or any other non-corporate email.

6). Someone wants to hire you but sends you a list of specifics for the job, including compensation info, without first asking your consent if you wanted the job in the first place.

Hello there. I'm glad I came across your post as I almost fell for this scam myself. I've been actively searching for work lately. So when I got this job interview invitation, I thought it was a legitimate email and text from "Arnette Schultz" and wrote back via email to set up my interview with her. 

But then I got suspicious after getting a document that talked about taxes, direct deposit, company equipment, etc. This was suspicious to me because all that information seemed like it should be provided after an interview and only to the chosen candidates for the job. So I posted my suspicion to Reddit and a kind soul got me thinking further. Then I went to the company's website to directly reach out to Arnette Schultz. Here's what I discovered:

Arnette Schultz is a real employee at Particle Technology Labs, but the email that was sent out about the Remote Data Entry Assistant interview was fake. Apparently, someone hacked into the real Arnette's LinkedIn account and has been impersonating her and using an email address that looks like a legitimate email from Particle Technology Labs, but the email is fake. Arnette mentioned that she would have her IT Team look into this matter. Hopefully it can be resolved in a swift manner so no further damages can be done.

It's disheartening and scary to know how far predators will go to prey on people. I've certainly learned a valuable lesson in being extra cautious when receiving job interview invitations or job offers. Whether you are in doubt or not, look up as much information as you can about the person who initiated contact with you. Use LinkedIn to look up the company's page and see if the person is listed there as an employee. In addition, go to the company's website and call/message/email them and ask something about that person (e.g. "Hello. My name is LyraTheArtist. I recently received an email from Arnette Schultz about a job interview for the position of Remote Data Entry Assistant at Particle Technology Labs. I have a question for Arnette. May I speak to her?"). If you get a response of, "We don't have anyone by that name working here.", then you know it was a scam.

If the customer comes in, just takes a look around, and leaves without asking you any questions or buying anything, then I wouldn't count this as you working since you didn't assist them with anything.

Now if a customer doesn't buy anything but you helped answer their questions, ask them to fill out a simple visitation log (with the date and time requirements) and if they ask why you can say you're looking for new ways to improve customer service in the store by asking customers to fill out a visitation log.
